explain.say: A real sorry says exactly what you did, uses a kind voice with no but, and offers to fix it. Well done! Here is a challenge: next time you make a mistake, try all five steps.

faq.q: What makes a sorry a real sorry?
faq.a: A real sorry says what you did, says sorry, shows you understand how they feel, tries to fix it and promises to do better. And no but!
asks: Tell me about the Say what you did
How do I say sorry properly?

faq.q: How can I fix things after I say sorry?
faq.a: Offer to help: rebuild the tower, replace the pencil, or invite them to play. Ask: What can I do to make it better?
asks: Tell me about the Fix it

faq.q: Why should I not say but in a sorry?
faq.a: Because but makes it sound like you are blaming them. Sorry, but you started it is really an excuse, not a sorry.
asks: Tell me about the Weak sorry

faq.q: What if they do not accept my sorry?
faq.a: Give them time; hurt feelings take a while to heal. Keep being kind, and they may be ready later.

faq.q: Should I say sorry if it was an accident?
faq.a: Yes. Saying sorry for an accident shows you care how the other person feels, even if you did not mean it.
asks: Do I say sorry for accidents?

facts: Research on apologies, including a 2016 study by Roy Lewicki, found that taking responsibility and offering to fix the problem are the most important parts of a good apology.
In Japan there are many ways to say sorry, from a casual "gomen" to a very polite "moushiwake arimasen".
